title: Build a Moving Box Calculator for Your Website Chatbot
summary: Build a moving box calculator for website chat. Give shoppers a box count and a matching kit link, then test shelf counts, fragile items and a catalog change.
body_markdown:
“I have two filled bookcases and my desk supplies. Which kit should I look at?” The Packing Bench widget links the shopper to the **Workroom kit** . Its packing list matches the reply item for item. There are **8 small boxes, 4 medium boxes and 2 rolls of tape** .


You’ll build this **moving box calculator for website chat** using one fictional retailer’s guide. Change the contents of those same two bookcases from books to fragile glass and the right answer changes. The shopper needs packing advice this time. You can[browse the demo shop](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/demos/packing-bench/index.html) and check both destinations as you go.


[Download the Packing Bench practice shop](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/packing-bench-practice-kit.zip) . It includes the shop pages, the exact Knowledge Base article and Main Prompt, and test messages. You can do the first four steps in a Quickchat AI account with credits for replies. For the website test, you’ll need a page you can edit. Personal practice fits the Free plan. A customer-facing shop needs a[plan with commercial use](https://quickchat.ai/docs/pricing-and-plans) . If you already have a widget, start with thecorrection and fragile-item tests .


## 1. What should your moving box calculator count?


Count **the contents of a full standard bookcase** . A shopper who says “two shelves” might mean two boards in one bookcase, or two whole bookcases. Those are different inputs. Packing Bench calls one full bookcase one *shelf unit* and includes ordinary desk supplies in each estimate.


*Read the guide from the shopper’s side. Count the bookcases being emptied. A fragile display or the desk itself goes straight to advice at any count.*


Full bookcases Kit in the demo shop Packed in the kit


0 or 1[Desk kit](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/demos/packing-bench/desk.html) (B-DESK) 4 small boxes, 2 medium boxes, 1 tape roll


2 or 3[Workroom kit](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/demos/packing-bench/workroom.html) (B-ROOM) 8 small boxes, 4 medium boxes, 2 tape rolls


4 or 5[Shared office kit](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/demos/packing-bench/shared-office.html) (B-PAIR) 12 small boxes, 6 medium boxes, 2 tape rolls


These numbers come from the demo catalog. A retailer following along should substitute its own tested bundles, exceptions and product URLs. Keeping the quantities together in one article gives you a single place to edit when a kit changes.


1. Sign in to the[Quickchat AI dashboard](https://app.quickchat.ai/) . If you already use an Agent, open the Agent switcher and choose **Add new AI Agent** to start a separate practice Agent. During setup, choose **Set up manually** , then name the Agent **Packing Bench** under **Identity** .
2. Go to **Knowledge Base → Add Article** . Title it **Home-office bundle table** . Paste the contents of` home-office-bundle-table.txt` from the download, or copy the text below. Each row includes the full address the shopper should open.
3. Save the article and wait for its status to read **Ready** . At that point the Agent can use it in both AI Preview and the website widget.[How Knowledge Base articles become available](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/knowledge-base) .


Copy the home-office bundle table


```text
One shelf unit means one filled standard bookcase. Count the contents you are packing, including ordinary desk supplies.


0 or 1 filled bookcase: Desk kit (B-DESK). 4 small boxes, 2 medium boxes, 1 tape roll.
Product page: https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/demos/packing-bench/desk.html


2 or 3 filled bookcases: Workroom kit (B-ROOM). 8 small boxes, 4 medium boxes, 2 tape rolls.
Product page: https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/demos/packing-bench/workroom.html


4 or 5 filled bookcases: Shared office kit (B-PAIR). 12 small boxes, 6 medium boxes, 2 tape rolls.
Product page: https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/demos/packing-bench/shared-office.html


Scope: The kits cover ordinary bookcase contents and desk supplies. For more than five filled bookcases, fragile displays or moving the desk itself, refer the shopper directly to our packing advice page: https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/demos/packing-bench/advice.html


For missing or partial bookcases, ask how many full standard bookcases' worth of ordinary contents they are packing. Never round a partial count. Treat each kit as a packing estimate.
```


The Ready status means the Agent can use the saved row and the exception beneath it.


## 2. How do you turn a shelf count into a product link?


Tell the Agent to check what’s on the shelves before it looks up a number. Two bookcases of paperbacks and two bookcases of glass occupy the same space in the shopper’s office. Only the paperbacks qualify for a standard kit under this guide.


In **Identity → AI Persona** , choose **Edit** on **Main Prompt** . Paste the contents of` main-prompt.txt` from the practice kit, then close the editor. The prompt saves automatically. The quantities stay in the article, so a change to a kit needs no prompt edit.


In AI Persona, open Main Prompt. Put the situations that need packing advice first.


Copy the full Main Prompt


```text
Use the Home-office bundle table for each packing estimate. Check the scope first. For more than five filled bookcases, fragile displays, or moving the desk itself, link the packing advice page without recommending a kit.


For ordinary desk supplies and bookcase contents, ask one short question if the count is missing or partial. Never round a partial count. For a covered count, name the kit, give its published small-box, medium-box and tape quantities, explain how you counted the bookcases, and link the product name to its exact page. Use the newest count if the shopper corrects it. Keep the reply short. Do not promise stock, delivery or a guaranteed fit.
```


Open **AI Preview** and ask **“I have two filled bookcases and my desk supplies. Which kit should I look at?”** Follow the link in the reply. Look for **B-ROOM** on the product page, then compare its three quantities with the answer. Here’s what the shopper saw when we ran the same test in the website widget.


The shopper can see which assumption produced this estimate.


The product page gives the shopper a second place to check the count.


## 3. When should the chatbot switch kits or send a shopper for advice?


Start a fresh chat with **“I have one filled standard bookcase and ordinary desk supplies. Which kit should I buy?”** After the Desk recommendation, send **“Actually, I left one out. I have two filled standard bookcases in total.”** Keep this pair in one conversation. In our test, the correction changed the link from Desk to Workroom and the estimate from 6 boxes to 12.


With just the three numeric rows in the article, our first test sent the fragile-glass shopper to Workroom with a handling caveat. When we asked about six bookcases, the Agent suggested combining two Workroom kits. Neither answer came from a published rule. We added the shop’s advice URL and exceptions to the article and put the scope check first in the Main Prompt. On separate reruns, both questions led to packing advice.


Try this in a fresh chat What to check


“I’m just packing desk supplies. Zero bookcases.” Desk kit, 4 small boxes, 2 medium boxes and 1 tape roll.


“Three full bookcases and ordinary desk supplies.” Workroom is still the matching kit.


“Four full bookcases.” Then try five in a new chat. Both counts select Shared office, with 12 small boxes, 6 medium boxes and 2 tape rolls.


“Six full bookcases.” The[packing advice page](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/demos/packing-bench/advice.html) . The published table ends at five.


“I’m packing my office.” Or “one bookcase and part of another.” A clarifying question before a product link. Let the shopper supply the count.


“Two bookcases of fragile glass displays.” Or “The desk itself needs to go too.” The advice link, even when the number would otherwise select a kit.


Four ordinary bookcases qualify for Shared office. The reply and product page agree on all three quantities.


For two bookcases of glass, the destination asks what needs packing and how large the pieces are.


## 4. How do you rerun all 11 packing questions?


A change that fixes the glass-display answer could also change what the Agent says about ordinary books. Save the questions together so you can check both cases after your next edit.


1. Open **Conversations → Testing → Create Dataset** . In **Dataset name** , enter **Packing Bench boundaries** .
2. Select **Paste messages** and paste the contents of` test-messages.txt` from the download. Each separator must be a line containing only` ---` . When the counter below the text reads **11 messages** , choose **Create** .


One line with three hyphens separates two shoppers’ questions. The count lets you check the whole file before starting a run.


1. Open the dataset and choose **Run** . Review the credit estimate and select **Start Run** . When the replies are ready, compare each one with the packing table and open its link when it gives one. The one-to-two correction still belongs in a single chat because the Agent needs the shopper’s earlier count.[Running a simulation](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/testing) .


## 5. How do you put the calculator on a shop page?


Install the floating **Widget** on a page you control. The public Packing Bench pages let anyone inspect the catalog. Your own copy is where you can install your own Agent and change the products.


1. Unzip the practice shop. Upload the contents of its` shop` folder together to a test site you can edit. Open` index.html` there and follow **Workroom kit** to check the address. Replace the four demo URLs in your Knowledge Base article with the full URLs on your test site. Save and wait for **Ready** .
2. In Quickchat AI, open **Channels → Your Website → Install → Install manually with code** . Copy your **Widget** snippet. Paste it immediately before` </body>` in the shop’s HTML pages. If you use a site builder, add it once in the site-wide footer or body-end code setting, then publish your test page.[Website widget installation](https://quickchat.ai/docs/channels/website) .


Choose Install manually with code, then copy the Widget snippet for the floating chat.


1. Open the shop in a private browser window and ask about **two full bookcases and ordinary desk supplies** . Click the Workroom link in the reply. Check that it opens *your* product page and that the counts agree.


The visitor can read the shop’s guide and ask for a kit on the same page.


1. Back in Quickchat AI, open **Inbox** and search for a distinctive phrase from the visitor’s message. Open the matching conversation. **Why AI said that** beneath the reply lets you inspect which knowledge the Agent used.[Finding a conversation in Inbox](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/inbox) .


The same conversation in Inbox. Link Clicked records which product the visitor opened.


## 6. What happens when the box count on the product page changes?


Try one catalog edit **on your practice copy** . Give the Workroom kit **5 medium boxes** . Keep its 8 small boxes, 2 tape rolls and B-ROOM identifier the same.


1. Change the medium-box count on your Workroom page and its listing. Open the product URL directly and check that it displays **5** .
2. Edit the Workroom row in **Home-office bundle table** to say **5 medium boxes** . Save it, wait for **Ready** , then start a fresh widget chat and ask the original two-bookcase question.
3. Compare the reply with the open product page. In our fresh website chat, the reply and the opened B-ROOM page both showed **5 medium boxes** . Restore **4** on the shop pages and in the article when you finish the test.


Fresh answer after editing the article.


The practice product page after the one-box change.


A manually written Knowledge Base article and a storefront are separate records. That matters beyond box counts. If a shopper needs today’s stock, connect a current catalog lookup. The[Shopify shopping assistant tutorial](https://quickchat.ai/post/shopify-ai-shopping-assistant) walks through a product search against a store catalog.


### Can ChatGPT or Claude prepare the setup?


Connect your Quickchat AI account through the[ChatGPT app](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a4656c688748191be4c5247fb0d5dfc) or the[Claude connector](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/app-quickchat-ai) . Give it the table and prompt from the download, then ask it to prepare the Agent. You’ll still need access to the site editor to install the widget.[Managing Quickchat AI from an AI client](https://quickchat.ai/docs/manage-with-ai) .


> Set up a practice Agent named Packing Bench. Use the attached Home-office bundle table and Main Prompt. Prepare test messages for one, two, five and six full bookcases, plus two bookcases of fragile glass. Show the expected link for each before running the tests.


## Moving box calculator FAQ


### How many moving boxes does the calculator suggest for two full bookcases?


In the Packing Bench example, two full bookcases of ordinary contents plus desk supplies select the Workroom kit. It contains 12 boxes in total, 8 small and 4 medium, plus 2 rolls of tape. That estimate comes from the fictional retailer’s guide.


### Can a moving box calculator estimate a whole apartment from the number of rooms?


This guide covers a home office and uses filled bookcases as its input. To cover an apartment, publish a separate guide that defines its rooms, assumptions, kit sizes and exceptions, then test the chatbot against those rules.


### What if the shopper only knows how many individual shelves they have?


Ask how many full standard bookcases’ worth of contents they are packing. An individual shelf has no fixed conversion in this guide. If the shopper cannot give a whole count, the shop’s packing advice page is available for an individual estimate.


### Can the chatbot recommend a kit for fragile items?


Packing Bench routes fragile displays, a move that includes the desk itself, and loads above five full bookcases to its packing advice page. On your store, link to a page that explains how the shopper can get an individual estimate.


### Do I need Shopify or a live inventory feed to use this on my website?


A website that can host the Quickchat AI Widget and has public kit pages is enough for this lookup. A fixed guide supplies the kit contents. To quote current stock or a shipping date, the Agent needs a source that can look those up at the time of the question.


### Can shoppers buy the recommended boxes in the chat?


This setup opens the recommended kit’s product page. On your store, shoppers can review the bundle and use your usual cart and checkout. The Packing Bench demo ends at the product page.
